title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 9–18. New: CISA on Nov. 17 added Perforce Puppet Enterprise CVE-2026-115731 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, due Dec. 1, and urged an immediate patch for Oracle Java CVE-2026-114938, which it calls Java4Shell. The Java alert does not list that bug in the catalog. Cisco, Outlook, Openwave, and Chromium entries from the Nov. 10 alert remain due Nov. 24. Barracuda CVE-2026-111560 and CVE-2026-116606 were due Nov. 13.

items.headline: CISA adds an exploited Puppet Enterprise flaw, due Dec. 1
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 17 that it added CVE-2026-115731, a Perforce Puppet Enterprise deserialization flaw, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation. The catalog says a client with any certificate-authority-signed agent certificate can execute code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a crafted report, and that if the authority autosigns certificates, an unauthenticated attacker can obtain one. CISA lists a due date of Dec. 1, 2026, says ransomware use is unknown, and does not require forensic triage. The catalog entry links Perforce's advisory.

items.headline: CISA adds Cisco, Barracuda, Openwave, Outlook, and Chromium bugs to KEV
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 10 it added six vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog: CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks, CVE-2026-111560 and CVE-2026-116606 in Barracuda Networks products, CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder, CVE-2026-124194 in Microsoft Office Outlook, and CVE-2026-125350 in Google Chromium. The catalog sets a due date of Nov. 13 for both Barracuda entries and requires forensic triage; it says the command-injection bug and the email-gateway authentication bypass can be chained. The other four are due Nov. 24, do not require forensic triage, and list ransomware use as unknown. CISA said the BroadWorks bug could let an unauthenticated remote attacker read configuration information, the Outlook bug could allow spoofing over a network, and the Chromium bug could allow code execution inside the sandbox via a crafted webpage, including in Chrome, Edge, and Opera.

items.headline: Cybersecurity Dive: Arctic Wolf says AntiFox attacks stole AWS credentials
items.summary: Cybersecurity Dive reported Nov. 13 that Arctic Wolf said Tuesday it uncovered attacks using the Alibaba-hosted AntiFox pen-testing framework to steal Amazon Web Services credentials. Cybersecurity Dive said at least two organizations were confirmed compromised and that researchers suspect six others were affected. Justin Moore of Arctic Wolf told Cybersecurity Dive the activity appears opportunistic and that the actors used AI-enabled tooling to increase the speed and scale of attacks against exposed web infrastructure and previously compromised credentials. An Amazon spokesperson told Cybersecurity Dive that AWS services were not specifically compromised and that the attackers used credentials taken from compromised applications to reach AWS accounts.

items.headline: The Hacker News: a jailbroken model exploited BroadWorks at a European telecom
items.summary: The Hacker News reported Nov. 11 that a campaign Malbear Labs calls Operation Snowball used an autonomous framework built on a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash model to exploit CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XML external entity flaw in Cisco BroadWorks, against a European telecommunications provider and 13 companies on its infrastructure. The Hacker News said Malbear Labs reported the agent enumerated hundreds of assets, extracted dozens of credential sets, and took thousands of rows of subscriber billing and device records over about two weeks. It said the primary target was a BroadWorks Xtended Services Platform, Release 23.0.1.1075, on port 2208, and that the agent recovered the system identity private key, three SSL credential sets, and three other private keys. The Hacker News said federal civilian agencies are recommended to patch by Nov. 24.

items.headline: CISA urges an immediate patch for Java4Shell in the HotSpot JVM
items.summary: CISA said Nov. 17 that organizations should immediately patch Oracle Java CVE-2026-114938, which it calls Java4Shell, a memory-corruption bug in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java virtual machine. CISA said specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA told defenders to find JDKs and Java runtimes, including copies bundled in applications, containers, and appliances, and to patch internet-facing systems first. The alert does not say the flaw is in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security contributed to it.

items.headline: FBI FLASH: Gootloader on more than 1,000 WordPress sites preceded $28 million in ransom
items.summary: The FBI released a Nov. 16 FLASH, coordinated with CISA and marked TLP:CLEAR, on Gootloader, a JavaScript loader that uses compromised websites and search-engine optimization for initial access. The FBI said cyber actors used it as a ransomware precursor across a wide variety of sectors, and that as of October 2026 it had identified over 1,000 infected WordPress sites and 216 domains controlled by the Gootloader administrator, which led to over $28 million in ransomware payments. The FLASH says activity from 2025 to 2026 has focused on U.S. legal professionals and legal-technology decision makers, and that the administrator scanned WordPress sites for xmlrpc.php and later used compromised credentials.

items.headline: Unit 42: Cairn and Chinese models hit semiconductor and defense targets
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 said Chinese-speaking attackers used the open-source Cairn framework, paired with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models, to run 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in August and September 2026. Unit 42 said the attackers achieved unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 organizations, including dozens of valid credentials, more than one million personal records at one organization, and military and government identities. Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that the activity, tracked as CL-STA-1238, is China-nexus intelligence collection, and said defense targets included a space technology company, a defense-analytics vendor, and a policy think tank. Cybersecurity Dive reported Nov. 13 that Unit 42 released the report on Thursday.

items.headline: Army CID asks industry for AI tools to watch the darknet and encrypted messaging
items.summary: DefenseScoop reported Nov. 12 that Army Criminal Investigation Division released a request for information for a cloud-hosted commercial platform that would use behavioral analytics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to monitor the darknet and encrypted messaging services, including Signal, Telegram, and Discord. The request says adversaries have left mainstream sites to plan hostile actions against Department of War personnel, high-value assets, and Army infrastructure. DefenseScoop said the capability matrix asks for tools that flag early signs of mobilization to violence, link anonymous accounts across platforms, and archive deleted or short-lived content. Industry responses are due Dec. 9.
